dossier_meta.paper: On symmetric intersecting families of vectors
dossier_meta.catalog_title: Size of symmetric intersecting families in $[k]^n$
dossier_meta.statement_text: How large can a symmetric, intersecting subfamily of $[k]^n$ really be (for fixed $k \geq 3$)?
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.1 establishes that any symmetric intersecting $A \subset [k]^n$ has size $o(k^n)$, but the precise asymptotics remain open. The best constructions known to the authors are set-intersecting families, e.g., those based on lines of a projective plane $PG(2,q)$, yielding size roughly $k^{n-\sqrt{n}}$.
